gaps.reason: Buildings and doors keep Tenth Spring original art by design.
The ROM has no marsh art: its one wetland is plain pale lawn dotted with ponds, and the puddle and shallow-water pieces are water edges or pale lawn, so every candidate would be a stand-in.
No railway track piece exists; the nearest look-alikes are fences, bridge decks and girders, none a track. A road piece is not a stand-in.
No path piece shows weeds on its surface; the lawn rim on edge pieces is a border, not weeds.
Every ROM path is at least two tiles wide, so there is no end, isolated or one-wide piece.
No cracked or broken paving piece exists in any paving family.
Every ROM street lane is at least two tiles wide, so there is no end, isolated or one-wide piece.
No paving piece shows weeds or grass tufts across its surface.
No headstone or grave marker piece was found on plain ground in any tileset.
The ROM's only pointed tree is a 2 x 2 block: there is no single-cell, row, column or grove piece, and a round canopy would be a stand-in.
No fence T-junction or crossing piece exists.
Water one tile wide with land on both sides: every pond edge piece shows a shore on one side or on two adjacent sides, none on two opposite sides.
Water with a single water neighbour (a channel end or peninsula tip, shore on three sides): the pond shore set has no three-sided end piece, and the sea-coloured beach pieces would be a stand-in.
An isolated one-tile pool: no pond-coloured piece draws a shore on all four sides.

The ROM's plank bridge is a deck exactly two tiles wide built of paired pieces: there is no plank piece for a one-tile deck or a single cell, and the inside of a wider deck (mask 15) cannot tell a north-south deck from an east-west one.
The only large rock pile sits on a cave floor, not on lawn, so it would read as a patch; the placeholder stays.
No outdoor park or towpath bench metatile exists across pri00 or sec01-sec15; 2x1 procedural stand-in draws until custom Decision 71 bench art.
No masonry canal lock gate metatile exists in the ROM; 2x3 procedural timber miter gates span the 3-tile canal channel until custom Decision 71 lock gate art.
